title: UTI in Pregnancy — Fluoroquinolone Contraindication
patient: Pregnant female, second trimester, dysuria, anxious about baby's health
diagnosis: Urinary Tract Infection — complicated (pregnancy = complicated UTI regardless of anatomy)

vitals.status: stable, afebrile, no flank pain or nausea (lower UTI, not pyelonephritis)

hpi: Pregnant female presents with dysuria. No fever, no flank pain, no nausea — consistent with lower UTI/cystitis rather than pyelonephritis. Repeatedly expresses concern about the baby's health.

missed.why: Dysuria in young female = STI on differential. Prompt treatment prevents harm to baby.
Patient repeatedly expressed anxiety about baby's health. Must address this directly.
Short-course antibiotic to minimize fetal exposure. Must be guided by culture sensitivities.
Stress importance of completing antibiotic course to prevent resistance.

avoided.why: CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY. Teratogenic — fetal cartilage damage. Despite being sensitive on culture, cannot be used.
First trimester: neural tube defects (folate antagonism). Third trimester: kernicterus risk (displaces bilirubin). High E. coli resistance anyway.

nitrofurantoin.note: Avoid first trimester (cardiac defects), avoid near delivery (hemolytic anemia in newborn)

cephalexin.note: Safe, but culture showed resistance in this case

complication.type: Complicated UTI — pregnancy = automatic complicated classification
complication.risk: Increased risk of pyelonephritis → preterm birth, low birth weight
complication.asymptomaticBacteriuria: Treated in pregnancy even without symptoms — two consecutive positive cultures = treat

timing.note: 1 negative patient update before correct treatment
